title: Prepare care preferences and practice respectful accompaniment

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: Respectful accompaniment follows the person’s actual preference and leaves symptoms and treatment with the care team. A conversation about future care preferences is preparation; its legal status depends on the relevant process and is not established by a worksheet.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Fictional adult Kai asks for understandable information, relief from discomfort and control over visitors. In a permitted visit Kai says, “Five minutes of quiet would help. Please ask the nurse about this discomfort; do not invite my relative.” The nurse is reachable through the established call route. No diagnosis, medicine or prognosis is supplied.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Choose the next actions and language, preserving the refusal and the care-team role. Separate this visit from any legal advance-care documentation.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: A patient ends a welcome visit early. May the visitor insist on finishing a comforting script because it was agreed before the visit?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: Offer the requested quiet, use the established route for the nurse, and do not invite the relative. Later fiction: nurse receives the request; no symptom outcome is supplied. Partial: quiet company but omit the requested contact. Incorrect: promise relief, prescribe treatment or organize reconciliation. Personal preferences can be written privately for discussion with the relevant care/legal process; this exercise creates no legally effective document.
criteria: The person’s current preferences govern accompaniment
Clinical and legal authority are not invented

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: No. The current preference governs continued company. End respectfully and convey any requested practical issue through the appropriate route; a script does not override withdrawal.
